sanskrit: yadā niyatikārpaṇyam athaiṣām eva rocate na hy atyantaṃ dhanavanto bhavanti sukhino 'pi vā
english: But when fate's stinginess falls upon them, then this very precept pleases them—for those who are rich are not, after all, forever happy.

sanskrit: yad anyair vihitaṃ necched ātmanaḥ karma pūruṣaḥ na tat pareṣu kurvīta jānann apriyam ātmanaḥ
english: Whatever deed a man would not wish others to do to him, that let him not do to others, knowing it would be hateful to himself.

sanskrit: yo 'nyasya syād upapatiḥ sa kaṃ kiṃ vaktum arhati yad anyas tasya tat kuryān na mṛṣyed iti me matiḥ
english: He who is another man's paramour—what right has he to reproach anyone? Were another to do the like to him, he would not endure it: such is my conviction.

sanskrit: jīvituṃ yaḥ svayaṃ cecchet kathaṃ so 'nyaṃ praghātayet yad yad ātmana iccheta tat parasyāpi cintayet
english: He who himself wishes to live—how could he slay another? Whatever a man would desire for himself, that let him intend for his fellow too.

sanskrit: atiriktaiḥ saṃvibhajed bhogair anyān akiṃcanān etasmāt kāraṇād dhātrā kusīdaṃ saṃpravartitam
english: With one's surplus enjoyments one should share with others who have nothing; for this very reason the Ordainer set lending at interest in motion.

sanskrit: yasmiṃs tu devāḥ samaye saṃtiṣṭheraṃs tathā bhavet atha cel lābhasamaye sthitir dharme 'pi śobhanā
english: As to the compact in which the gods would abide, so let it be; and if even in a time of gain one keeps to dharma, that constancy is fair indeed.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ priyābhyupagataṃ dharmam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ paśyaitaṃ lakṣaṇoddeśaṃ dharmādharme yudhiṣṭhira
english: The wise declare that all dharma is grounded in what is dear and welcome; behold this marking-out of the signs of dharma and of its opposite, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: lokasaṃgrahasaṃyuktaṃ vidhātrā vihitaṃ purā sūkṣmadharmārthaniyataṃ satāṃ caritam uttamam
english: Bound up with the holding-together of the world, ordained of old by the Disposer, fixed upon the subtle aim of dharma—such is the supreme conduct of the good.

sanskrit: dharmalakṣaṇam ākhyātam etat te kurusattama tasmād anārjave buddhir na kāryā te kathaṃ cana
english: This mark of dharma has now been told to you, O best of the Kurus; therefore let your mind never in any way incline toward crookedness.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sūkṣmaṃ sādhu samādiṣṭaṃ bhavatā dharmalakṣaṇam pratibhā tv asti me kā cit tāṃ brūyām anumānataḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Subtle and well has the mark of dharma been set forth by you; yet a certain notion stirs in me, which I would utter by way of inference.

sanskrit: bhūyāṃso hṛdaye ye me praśnās te vyāhṛtās tvayā imam anyaṃ pravakṣyāmi na rājan vigrahād iva
english: The many questions that were in my heart you have answered; this further one I shall now put—not, O king, in any spirit of contention.

sanskrit: imāni hi prāpayanti sṛjanty uttārayanti ca na dharmaḥ paripāṭhena śakyo bhārata veditum
english: These [precepts] indeed bring men onward, set them forth, and carry them across; yet dharma cannot be known, O Bhārata, by mere rote recitation.

sanskrit: anyo dharmaḥ samasthasya viṣamasthasya cāparaḥ āpadas tu kathaṃ śakyāḥ paripāṭhena veditum
english: One dharma belongs to the man in easy circumstances, another to him in dire straits; how then can times of calamity be understood by rote?

sanskrit: sadācāro mato dharmaḥ santas tv ācāralakṣaṇāḥ sādhyāsādhyaṃ kathaṃ śakyaṃ sadācāro hy alakṣaṇam
english: Right conduct is held to be dharma, and the good are known by their conduct; but how can the attainable and the unattainable be told apart, when right conduct itself bears no fixed sign?

sanskrit: dṛśyate dharmarūpeṇa adharmaṃ prākṛtaś caran dharmaṃ cādharmarūpeṇa kaś cid aprākṛtaś caran
english: One sees a common man practicing unrighteousness under the guise of righteousness, and some uncommon man practicing righteousness under the guise of unrighteousness.

sanskrit: punar asya pramāṇaṃ hi nirdiṣṭaṃ śāstrakovidaiḥ vedavādāś cānuyugaṃ hrasantīti ha naḥ śrutam
english: Again, its standard has been laid down by those versed in the scriptures; yet we have heard it said that the teachings of the Vedas dwindle age by age.

sanskrit: anye kṛtayuge dharmās tretāyāṃ dvāpare 'pare anye kaliyuge dharmā yathāśaktikṛtā iva
english: One set of dharmas held in the Kṛta age, another in the Tretā, and others in the Dvāpara; other dharmas hold in the Kali age, framed as it were to suit men's diminished powers.

sanskrit: āmnāyavacanaṃ satyam ity ayaṃ lokasaṃgrahaḥ āmnāyebhyaḥ paraṃ vedāḥ prasṛtā viśvatomukhāḥ
english: "The word of sacred tradition is truth"—this is what holds the world together; yet beyond the traditions the Vedas have streamed forth, facing in every direction.

sanskrit: te cet sarve pramāṇaṃ vai pramāṇaṃ tan na vidyate pramāṇe cāpramāṇe ca viruddhe śāstratā kutaḥ
english: If they are all authoritative, then there is no [single] authority to be found; and when authority and non-authority stand in mutual contradiction, whence the standing of scripture itself?

sanskrit: dharmasya hriyamāṇasya balavadbhir durātmabhiḥ yā yā vikriyate saṃsthā tataḥ sāpi praṇaśyati
english: When dharma is being carried off by the strong and the wicked, whatever ordinance is thereby corrupted—that ordinance too perishes.

sanskrit: vidma caivaṃ na vā vidma śakyaṃ vā vedituṃ na vā aṇīyān kṣuradhārāyā garīyān parvatād api
english: Whether we know it thus or know it not, whether it can be known or cannot—[dharma] is finer than the razor's edge and heavier than a mountain.

sanskrit: gandharvanagarākāraḥ prathamaṃ saṃpradṛśyate anvīkṣyamāṇaḥ kavibhiḥ punar gacchaty adarśanam
english: At first it appears with the shape of a gandharva's city in the sky; but when the wise look closely upon it, it passes again into invisibility.

sanskrit: nipānānīva gobhyāśe kṣetre kulyeva bhārata smṛto 'pi śāśvato dharmo viprahīṇo na dṛśyate
english: Like watering-troughs near a herd of cattle, like a channel in a field, O Bhārata—even the eternal dharma, though remembered, once forsaken is no more seen.

sanskrit: kāmād anye kṣayād anye kāraṇair aparais tathā asanto hi vṛthācāraṃ bhajante bahavo 'pare
english: Some from desire, some from ruin, and others yet from sundry causes—many of the wicked, and others besides, take to empty and worthless conduct.

sanskrit: dharmo bhavati sa kṣipraṃ vilīnas tv eva sādhuṣu anye tān āhur unmattān api cāvahasanty uta
english: Dharma soon comes to be, yet it lies dissolved [unseen] within the good; others call such good men madmen, and even mock them.

sanskrit: mahājanā hy upāvṛttā rājadharmaṃ samāśritāḥ na hi sarvahitaḥ kaś cid ācāraḥ saṃpradṛśyate
english: For the multitudes have turned away, taking refuge in the law of kings; and no single mode of conduct is seen that is for the good of all.

sanskrit: tenaivānyaḥ prabhavati so 'paraṃ bādhate punaḥ dṛśyate caiva sa punas tulyarūpo yadṛcchayā
english: By that very [conduct] another arises, and he in turn oppresses yet another; and again he is seen, by mere chance, in the selfsame form.

sanskrit: yenaivānyaḥ prabhavati so 'parān api bādhate ācārāṇām anaikāgryaṃ sarveṣām eva lakṣayet
english: By the very means whereby one man rises, he oppresses others too; one should mark the want of single-pointedness in all modes of conduct alike.

sanskrit: cirābhipannaḥ kavibhiḥ pūrvaṃ dharma udāhṛtaḥ tenācāreṇa pūrveṇa saṃsthā bhavati śāśvatī
english: Long ago attained by the seers, dharma was set forth of old; and by that ancient mode of conduct the ordinance abides eternal.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam tulādhārasya vākyāni dharme jājalinā saha
english: Bhīṣma said: On this point too they recite this ancient tale—the words of Tulādhāra concerning dharma, in his exchange with Jājali.

sanskrit: vane vanacaraḥ kaś cij jājalir nāma vai dvijaḥ sāgaroddeśam āgamya tapas tepe mahātapāḥ
english: A certain forest-dwelling brahmin named Jājali, that great ascetic, having come to a spot beside the ocean, practiced austerities there.

sanskrit: niyato niyatāhāraś cīrājinajaṭādharaḥ malapaṅkadharo dhīmān bahūn varṣagaṇān muniḥ
english: Self-controlled and of measured fare, wearing bark-cloth, hide, and matted locks, smeared with dirt and grime, the wise sage [endured] for many a cycle of years.

sanskrit: sa kadā cin mahātejā jalavāso mahīpate cacāra lokān viprarṣiḥ prekṣamāṇo manojavaḥ
english: Once, O lord of earth, that brahmin-seer of mighty splendor, dwelling in the waters, ranged through the worlds, beholding them, swift as thought.

sanskrit: sa cintayām āsa munir jalamadhye kadā cana viprekṣya sāgarāntāṃ vai mahīṃ savanakānanām
english: On a certain occasion the sage, standing amid the waters, took to musing, as he gazed upon the earth bounded by the ocean, with its groves and forests:

sanskrit: na mayā sadṛśo 'stīha loke sthāvarajaṅgame apsu vaihāyasaṃ gacchen mayā yo 'nyaḥ saheti vai
english: "There is none in this world, among things moving or unmoving, who is my equal—who else along with me could pass through the waters and through the air?"

sanskrit: sa dṛśyamāno rakṣobhir jalamadhye 'vadat tataḥ abruvaṃś ca piśācās taṃ naivaṃ tvaṃ vaktum arhasi
english: Then, being observed by the rākṣasas as he stood amid the waters, he spoke thus; and the piśācas said to him, "You ought not to speak in this manner.

sanskrit: tulādhāro vaṇigdharmā vārāṇasyāṃ mahāyaśāḥ so 'py evaṃ nārhate vaktuṃ yathā tvaṃ dvijasattama
english: Tulādhāra, a merchant by calling, of great renown in Vārāṇasī—even he does not deserve to speak as you do, O best of the twice-born."

sanskrit: ity ukto jājalir bhūtaiḥ pratyuvāca mahātapāḥ paśyeyaṃ tam ahaṃ prājñaṃ tulādhāraṃ yaśasvinam
english: Thus addressed by those beings, the great ascetic Jājali replied: "Let me behold that wise and illustrious Tulādhāra."

sanskrit: iti bruvāṇaṃ tam ṛṣiṃ rakṣāṃsy uddhṛtya sāgarāt abruvan gaccha panthānam āsthāyemaṃ dvijottama
english: As that seer spoke thus, the rākṣasas lifted him up out of the ocean and said, "Go, taking this road, O best of the twice-born."

sanskrit: ity ukto jājalir bhūtair jagāma vimanās tadā vārāṇasyāṃ tulādhāraṃ samāsādyābravīd vacaḥ
english: Thus addressed by those beings, Jājali then set forth downcast, and approaching Tulādhāra in Vārāṇasī, he spoke these words.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kiṃ kṛtaṃ sukṛtaṃ karma tāta jājalinā purā yena siddhiṃ parāṃ prāptas tan no vyākhyātum arhasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What meritorious deed had Jājali done of old, dear sir, whereby he attained the highest perfection? That you ought to explain to us.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atīva tapasā yukto ghoreṇa sa babhūva ha nadyupasparśanarataḥ sāyaṃ prātar mahātapāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: He had become exceedingly devoted to fearsome austerity, that great ascetic, given to bathing in the river at evening and at dawn,

sanskrit: agnīn paricaran samyak svādhyāyaparamo dvijaḥ vānaprasthavidhānajño jājalir jvalitaḥ śriyā
english: duly tending the sacred fires, intent above all on the recitation of scripture—that brahmin Jājali, versed in the rule of the forest-hermit, blazing with spiritual splendor.

sanskrit: satye tapasi tiṣṭhan sa na ca dharmam avaikṣata varṣāsv ākāśaśāyī sa hemante jalasaṃśrayaḥ
english: Steadfast in truth and austerity, yet he did not [truly] perceive dharma; in the rains he lay beneath the open sky, in winter he took to the water,

sanskrit: vatātapasaho grīṣme na ca dharmam avindata duḥkhaśayyāś ca vividhā bhūmau ca parivartanam
english: in summer enduring wind and scorching sun—and still he did not find dharma; he bore beds of pain of many kinds, and rolling upon the bare earth.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cit sa munir varṣāsv ākāśam āsthitaḥ antarikṣāj jalaṃ mūrdhnā pratyagṛhṇān muhur muhuḥ
english: Then once, during the rains, that sage took his stand beneath the open sky and received the water from the firmament upon his head, again and again.

sanskrit: atha tasya jaṭāḥ klinnā babhūvur grathitāḥ prabho araṇyagamanān nityaṃ malino malasaṃyutāḥ
english: Then his matted locks grew sodden and tangled, O lord, and from his constant ranging in the wild ever filthy and caked with dirt.

sanskrit: sa kadā cin nirāhāro vāyubhakṣo mahātapāḥ tasthau kāṣṭhavad avyagro na cacāla ca karhi cit
english: Then once that great ascetic, taking no food and feeding on air alone, stood still as a log, unmoved, and stirred not at all.

sanskrit: tasya sma sthāṇubhūtasya nirviceṣṭasya bhārata kuliṅgaśakunau rājan nīḍaṃ śirasi cakratuḥ
english: While he stood thus, become like a tree-stump, motionless, O Bhārata—a pair of kuliṅga sparrows, O king, made a nest upon his head.

sanskrit: sa tau dayāvān viprarṣir upapraikṣata dampatī kurvāṇaṃ nīḍakaṃ tatra jaṭāsu tṛṇatantubhiḥ
english: That compassionate brahmin-seer watched the mated pair as they fashioned their little nest there in his matted locks with strands of grass.

sanskrit: yadā sa na calaty eva sthāṇubhūto mahātapāḥ tatas tau pariviśvastau sukhaṃ tatroṣatus tadā
english: And since that great ascetic, become like a stump, stirred not at all, the two birds, grown wholly trusting, dwelt there in ease.

sanskrit: atītāsv atha varṣāsu śaratkāla upasthite prājāpatyena vidhinā viśvāsāt kāmamohitau
english: Then, when the rains had passed and the autumn season had come, the pair, made trusting and overcome by desire, after the manner ordained of Prajāpati,

sanskrit: tatrāpātayatāṃ rājañ śirasy aṇḍāni khecarau tāny abudhyata tejasvī sa vipraḥ saṃśitavrataḥ
english: those two skyfarers, O king, let fall their eggs upon his head; and that splendid brahmin of strict vows became aware of them.

sanskrit: buddhvā ca sa mahātejā na cacālaiva jājaliḥ dharme dhṛtamanā nityaṃ nādharmaṃ sa tv arocayat
english: And though aware, that mighty Jājali stirred not at all; his mind ever fixed upon dharma, he would not consent to unrighteousness.

sanskrit: ahany ahani cāgamya tatas tau tasya mūrdhani āśvāsitau vai vasataḥ saṃprahṛṣṭau tadā vibho
english: And day after day the two would come and dwell upon his head, reassured and full of joy, O mighty one.

sanskrit: aṇḍebhyas tv atha puṣṭebhyaḥ prajāyanta śakuntakāḥ vyavardhanta ca tatraiva na cākampata jājaliḥ
english: Then from the well-grown eggs the little birds were hatched, and they grew up in that very place; yet Jājali did not waver.

sanskrit: sa rakṣamāṇas tv aṇḍāni kuliṅgānāṃ yatavrataḥ tathaiva tasthau dharmātmā nirviceṣṭaḥ samāhitaḥ
english: Guarding the eggs of the kuliṅgas, that man of disciplined vows, the righteous one, stood thus motionless and composed.

sanskrit: tatas tu kālasamaye babhūvus te 'tha pakṣiṇaḥ bubudhe tāṃś ca sa munir jātapakṣāñ śakuntakān
english: Then in the fullness of time those fledglings grew into birds, and the sage marked the little ones now grown of wing.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cit tāṃs tatra paśyan pakṣīn yatavrataḥ babhūva paramaprītas tadā matimatāṃ varaḥ
english: Then once, beholding those birds there, that man of disciplined vows, the best of the wise, became filled with the highest delight.

sanskrit: tathā tān abhisaṃvṛddhān dṛṣṭvā cāpnuvatāṃ mudam śakunau nirbhayau tatra ūṣatuś cātmajaiḥ saha
english: Seeing them thus full-grown, the pair of parent birds attained their joy and dwelt there fearless, together with their offspring.

sanskrit: jātapakṣāṃś ca so 'paśyad uḍḍīnān punarāgatān sāyaṃ sāyaṃ dvijān vipro na cākampata jājaliḥ
english: And the brahmin watched the fledged birds fly off and return again, evening after evening; yet Jājali did not waver.

sanskrit: kadā cit punar abhyetya punar gacchanti saṃtatam tyaktā mātṛpitṛbhyāṃ te na cākampata jājaliḥ
english: Sometimes coming back and going off again, unbroken in their comings—and at last forsaken by their mother and father—yet Jājali did not waver.

sanskrit: atha te divasaṃ cārīṃ gatvā sāyaṃ punar nṛpa upāvartanta tatraiva nivāsārthaṃ śakuntakāḥ
english: Then the little birds, having gone off by day to forage, would return again at evening, O king, to dwell in that selfsame place.

sanskrit: kadā cid divasān pañca samutpatya vihaṃgamāḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'hani samājagmur na cākampata jājaliḥ
english: Once the birds flew off for five days, and on the sixth day they came back together; yet Jājali did not waver.

sanskrit: krameṇa ca punaḥ sarve divasāni bahūny api nopāvartanta śakunā jātaprāṇāḥ sma te yadā
english: And by degrees, when those birds had come fully into their strength, they no longer returned for many days at a time.

sanskrit: kadā cin māsamātreṇa samutpatya vihaṃgamāḥ naivāgacchaṃs tato rājan prātiṣṭhata sa jājaliḥ
english: Once the birds flew off and for a whole month did not come back; thereupon, O king, Jājali set forth.

sanskrit: tatas teṣu pralīneṣu jājalir jātavismayaḥ siddho 'smīti matiṃ cakre tatas taṃ māna āviśat
english: Then, when they had vanished away, Jājali, filled with wonder, formed the thought "I am perfected"; and thereupon pride entered into him.

sanskrit: sa tathā nirgatān dṛṣṭvā śakuntān niyatavrataḥ saṃbhāvitātmā saṃbhāvya bhṛśaṃ prītas tadābhavan
english: Seeing the birds thus gone forth, that man of fixed vows, esteeming himself, took it for a high thing and became greatly pleased.

sanskrit: sa nadyāṃ samupaspṛśya tarpayitvā hutāśanam udayantam athādityam abhyagacchan mahātapāḥ
english: Having bathed in the river and gratified the fire with oblation, that great ascetic then went forth toward the rising sun.

sanskrit: saṃbhāvya caṭakān mūrdhni jājalir japatāṃ varaḥ āsphoṭayat tadākāśe dharmaḥ prāpto mayeti vai
english: Honoring [the memory of] the sparrows upon his head, Jājali, foremost of those who recite, clapped his arms then toward the sky [crying], "Dharma has been attained by me!"

sanskrit: athāntarikṣe vāg āsīt tāṃ sa śuśrāva jājaliḥ dharmeṇa na samas tvaṃ vai tulādhārasya jājale
english: Then there came a voice from the firmament, and Jājali heard it: "In dharma you are not the equal of Tulādhāra, O Jājali.

sanskrit: vārāṇasyāṃ mahāprājñas tulādhāraḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ so 'py evaṃ nārhate vaktuṃ yathā tvaṃ bhāṣase dvija
english: In Vārāṇasī dwells Tulādhāra, the man of great wisdom; even he does not deserve to speak as you speak, O brahmin."

sanskrit: so 'marṣavaśam āpannas tulādhāradidṛkṣayā pṛthivīm acarad rājan yatrasāyaṃgṛho muniḥ
english: Falling under the sway of indignation, in his longing to behold Tulādhāra, he ranged over the earth, O king—that sage who made his home wherever evening found him.

sanskrit: kālena mahatāgacchat sa tu vārāṇasīṃ purīm vikrīṇantaṃ ca paṇyāni tulādhāraṃ dadarśa saḥ
english: After a long while he came to the city of Vārāṇasī, and there he beheld Tulādhāra selling his wares.

sanskrit: so 'pi dṛṣṭvaiva taṃ vipram āyāntaṃ bhāṇḍajīvanaḥ samutthāya susaṃhṛṣṭaḥ svāgatenābhyapūjayat
english: And he too, the one who lived by his goods, no sooner saw that brahmin approaching than he rose up full of joy and honored him with a welcome.

sanskrit: tulādhāra uvāca āyān evāsi vidito mama brahman na saṃśayaḥ bravīmi yat tu vacanaṃ tac chṛṇuṣva dvijottama
english: Tulādhāra said: That you were coming was known to me, O brahmin—of that there is no doubt; hear now the word that I shall speak, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: sāgarānūpam āśritya tapas taptaṃ tvayā mahat na ca dharmasya saṃjñāṃ tvaṃ purā vettha kathaṃ cana
english: Resorting to the marshy shore of the ocean, you performed great austerity; and yet, before, you in no wise knew the very meaning of dharma.

sanskrit: tataḥ siddhasya tapasā tava vipra śakuntakāḥ kṣipraṃ śirasy ajāyanta te ca saṃbhāvitās tvayā
english: Then, O brahmin, when you had been perfected by your austerity, the little birds were quickly hatched upon your head, and they were cherished by you.

sanskrit: jātapakṣā yadā te ca gatāś cārīm itas tataḥ manyamānas tato dharmaṃ caṭakaprabhavaṃ dvija khe vācaṃ tvam athāśrauṣīr māṃ prati dvijasattama
english: And when, fledged at last, they went off here and there to forage—deeming then, O brahmin, that dharma had sprung from those sparrows—you heard a voice in the sky concerning me, O best of the twice-born;

sanskrit: amarṣavaśam āpannas tataḥ prāpto bhavān iha karavāṇi priyaṃ kiṃ te tad brūhi dvijasattama
english: and then, falling under the sway of indignation, you have come here. What kindness may I do you? Tell me that, O best of the twice-born.
